offers.name: Acer Aspire Lite 15 15.6" FHD Laptop - Intel Core 3 N350 - 16GB DDR4 - 512GB SSD - Windows 11 Home in S Mode - Silver

praises: N350 sips power: all-day-feel battery for browsing, docs, and streaming
16GB DDR4 is generous for an N-series machine and keeps everyday Windows smooth
Webcam has a physical privacy shutter — a small but appreciated touch
Runs completely cool and silent for typical light use
At the $719.99 sale it's a fine big-screen browser/streamer
complaints: Wi-Fi 5 (802.11ac) only in 2026 — the oldest wireless in the dataset and a real downgrade on modern routers
Ships in Windows 11 S Mode; leaving it is a clunky store dance that surprises non-technical buyers
N350 is 8 low-power E-cores: heavy spreadsheet, photo, or multitask work crawls
Port set is sparse: one USB-A 3.2, one USB 2.0, one USB-C
Regular $1,139.99 is absurd for N-series; only the sale price is honest

standouts: Long battery and silence for pure light use; webcam privacy shutter at this price
dealbreakers: Wi-Fi 5 + S Mode + weak N-series CPU: for a few dollars more the Core 5 120U or Ryzen SKUs are better machines in every way
design_philosophy: The floor of the Aspire Lite range: an Alder Lake-N E-core platform chosen purely for cost and efficiency, padded with 16GB DDR4 to mask how weak the CPU is, and trimmed with Wi-Fi 5 and Windows S Mode. It targets the most casual possible user — browser, email, video — and nothing beyond.
rating_notes: No pro review found (see SHARED-aspire-go.md). Platform-anchored on Alder Lake-N: productivity 3.5 (8 E-cores, weak single-thread), gaming 1.0 (24EU UHD), battery 6.8 estimated (capacity unpublished; N-series efficiency). Panel unstated → assumed TN per BUDGET_LIST rule. S Mode and Wi-Fi 5 verified from BBY listing; they justify the low port_connectivity/ecosystem friction notes (S Mode not scored separately).
